audit.whatIsWrong: The single most decisive interaction in this matchup is absent from every field: Meditate is a channel, and Riven's Ki Burst cancels it outright. The page mentions the stun four times and never once connects it to his heal.
audit.why: Meditate is a flat 10-second cooldown that restores health AND reduces damage taken AND stacks Double Strike AND pauses the duration on Wuju Style and Highlander. It is the reason a losing Yi survives a lost lane. A Riven who holds Ki Burst for the moment he starts channelling deletes all four of those benefits with one button — and a Riven who spends the stun on the approach watches him heal back everything she just did. That is the difference between a won lane and a stalled one, and it was nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[1], spikes[1].text, wants.you[1] and early: hold the stun for the channel, not for the approach.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere — needs concrete wait for X before you Y lines', and sequencingCues is 0. Not one cooldown number appears anywhere in the content layer.
audit.why: Alpha Strike is the cooldown this lane runs on and it behaves unusually: 20/19.5/19/18.5/18 seconds, but 'basic attacks reduce Alpha Strike's cooldown', so the real timer moves with how much he is hitting. It also makes him untargetable in flight, which means burst spent into it is thrown away — missingInteractions flags exactly this as untargetable-dodges-burst. A player told only 'he can Alpha through your combo' has no idea whether that is available now.
audit.corrected: mid rewritten as an explicit wait-for-X line: 20s at rank 1, untargetable mid-flight, and count his autos because they shave the cooldown. Wuju Style's 14s and Highlander's 85s added to whys[3] and whys[5], and wants.foe[1] tightened to name the untargetable dodge.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, and no acknowledgement that part of his damage ignores resistances.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags both. Meditate heals on a 10s cooldown, so Grievous Wounds is not a luxury in a long game — it is what stops him resetting a fight he already lost. And Wuju Style grants true damage on his basic attacks for 14s, which means stacking armour reads the trade wrong: the answer is to end the exchange inside a stun window, not to survive it.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named against Meditate in late; Wuju Style's true damage and 14s cooldown in whys[3] and early, with the explicit instruction to keep trades short.
